subject.title: [Bug] PTY silently disabled in sandbox mode without warning when pty:true is set

question: For explicit `pty: true` in sandboxed exec, should OpenClaw warn and continue without PTY, reject the tool call, or document the current silent fallback as intended?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the correct behavior changes how a denied sandbox capability is exposed to users and therefore needs maintainer security/product intent.

options.title: Warn And Continue
options.body: Emit a clear warning through the existing exec warnings channel while preserving current sandboxed non-PTY execution.

options.title: Fail Explicit PTY
options.body: Reject sandboxed exec calls that explicitly request PTY so users must choose another execution mode.

options.title: Document Current Behavior
options.body: Keep silent non-PTY sandbox execution and update docs to say PTY is best-effort and unavailable in sandbox mode.

recommendation.title: Warn And Continue
recommendation.body: Emit a clear warning through the existing exec warnings channel while preserving current sandboxed non-PTY execution.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest history on exec PTY support, fallback behavior, and docs/runtime routing.
